svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Market risk desk dashboard — Narrative Review variant, screen 1
svg.desc: Static desktop mockup of a market risk dashboard laid out as a three-act narrative. Act 1, What changed: a verdict banner states that one-day risk rose materially, showing VaR 99 percent one-day of 8.42 million dollars, up 1.26 million or 17.6 percent versus the prior day, alongside Expected Shortfall 97.5 percent one-day of 8.95 million dollars, an approximate VaR 99 percent ten-day figure of 26.6 million dollars scaled by the square root of ten, and 4 backtest exceptions over the trailing 250 days against an expected 2.5. Act 2, Why it moved: additive component VaR bars for Equity 4.86, Rates 1.94, Credit 1.02, FX 0.41 and Commodity 0.19 million dollars sum exactly to the 8.42 million total, with day-over-day change per component, and a separate reconciliation panel showing standalone VaR sum 11.87 million less a diversification benefit of 3.45 million. Act 3, The evidence: a simulated one-day profit and loss distribution with the VaR and Expected Shortfall thresholds marked in the loss tail, a 60-day backtest of daily profit and loss against the moving VaR threshold containing one exception, and an exception log listing all four exceptions of the trailing 250 days. A page-wide method selector set to Historical simulation governs every figure. All data is illustrative and synthetic.
svg.text: Illustrative / synthetic data · as-of 30 Sep 2026 · portfolio NAV $412.0M
METHOD — APPLIES TO EVERY FIGURE ON THIS PAGE
Lookback 500 days · full revaluation · switching method re-derives every figure
Risk is up materially — and it is concentrated.
One-day VaR rose 17.6% overnight, and one sleeve — Equity — explains 87% of
the increase. Read down the page: verdict, then cause, then proof.
Average loss in the worst 2.5% of simulated days
1-day figure scaled by √10 — approximation, not a re-simulation
Expected ≈ 2.5 at 99% confidence — see the log in Act 3
Component VaR is additive and reconciles exactly to the total.
Each bar is a marginal contribution to the 99% / 1-day total. Components sum to $8.42M with no residual.
29.1% of standalone risk is netted away by offsets
between sleeves. This benefit is never distributed
into the additive component figures above.
Equity notional grew 6% into a vol regime shift (18% → 24% ann.),
500 historical scenarios, full revaluation. The thresholds above are read off this tail.
Red bars mark the worst 1% of scenarios — the tail VaR 99% cuts off at its threshold.
ES 97.5% averages the worst 2.5%: a different, wider tail that here sits deeper in loss.
Daily clean P&L against that day's VaR threshold. 1 exception in this window; 4 in the trailing 250 days.
Every breach, with the attributed driver. This is the audit trail behind the “4 exceptions” figure in Act 1.
Rates repricing after a CPI surprise

Method & assumptions — Historical simulation, 500-day lookback, equally weighted, full revaluation, 1-day holding period. Component VaR is marginal and additive to the total; diversification is reported as a separate line.
The 10-day figure is a √10 scaling of the 1-day result and is labelled approximate throughout. All figures on this page are illustrative and synthetic, produced for interface design review only.
